newsitem.title: UK: More Russian off-grade aluminium arrives in Baltic.
newsitem.headline: More Russian off-grade aluminium arrives in Baltic.

text.p: A few more parcels of Russian off-grade aluminium have been arriving in Baltic ports, but not enough to satisfy pent-up demand and knock physical premiums, traders said.
A shortage of Russian off-grade metal since about last September has narrowed the differential between LME-deliverable A7E grade and the off-grades.
In Rotterdam the premium for A7E was around $30/$40 while A7 and A6 were only bout $5 and $10 less respectively.
"We have seen more (off-grade) metal being offered to us in the ports," a trader said. Grades that have been seen were AB99, AB97, A5 and A6, traders said.
"We think some of it has been finding a home in the States," one said.
Another trader said off-grades were still scarce.
"If you come in with 500 tonnes and someone is short it just goes where it is short. There's not really much trading," one trader said.
There was still very little of the A0 grade around, most traders said.
"The problem is getting it. As soon as we have some, it is very easy to sell it at a $5 to $10 premium," one said.
But another trader said A0 had gone to a $5 to $10 discount, adding it may have eased because India, usually a big buyer of the grade, had imposed import restrictions.
Some Russian aluminium was being shipped from East Coast ports directly to China by a big player in Russian aluminium, he added.
Overall, trade in physical aluminium had been muted, traders said.
The premiums for Western metal in Rotterdam were little changed at $40/$50 for duty unpaid and $125/$135 for duty paid.
